commit_message:
[VMVX] Added an implementation of fpowi in vm for vmvx backend (#24608)

We have found some models, which failed to compile to vmvx, due to a
missing conversion for math.fpowi.

This PR includes an implementation for this op, as well as an addition
of VM_ComplexArithmeticOp class, since fpowi has a float and int input.
This case was not covered by the VM_BinaryArithmeticOp class. However,
since we only found fpowi in models, which utilize a i64 const for the
exponent, the op was implemented in such a way that it only accepts i64
as an exponent. Due to this, it was not necessary to implement a
ComplexArithmeticOpConversion in
[MathToVM/Patterns.cpp](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/main/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Dialect/VM/Conversion/MathToVM/Patterns.cpp).

I also expanded the tests in arithmetic_ops.mlir, to include a check for
vm.fpowi.f32.

Signed-off-by: Hakan Eyilmez
[eyilmez@roofline.ai](mailto:eyilmez@roofline.ai)

---------

Signed-off-by: Hakan Eyilmez <eyilmez@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[VMVX] Added an implementation of fpowi in vm for vmvx backend (#24608)

We have found some models, which failed to compile to vmvx, due to a
missing conversion for math.fpowi.

This PR includes an implementation for this op, as well as an addition
of VM_ComplexArithmeticOp class, since fpowi has a float and int input.
This case was not covered by the VM_BinaryArithmeticOp class. However,
since we only found fpowi in models, which utilize a i64 const for the
exponent, the op was implemented in such a way that it only accepts i64
as an exponent. Due to this, it was not necessary to implement a
ComplexArithmeticOpConversion in
[MathToVM/Patterns.cpp](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/main/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Dialect/VM/Conversion/MathToVM/Patterns.cpp).

I also expanded the tests in arithmetic_ops.mlir, to include a check for
vm.fpowi.f32.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: scalable pack and unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: scalable pack and unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax, a static
distribution tile of a scalable pack/unpack is a whole multiple of the
inner tile for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack/unpack fused into a packed-domain root such as an mmt4d takes its
distribution tile from the root's outer dims, so map that onto the
unpacked domain first. The result is itself scalable, which lets its
multiplier be compared against the inner tile's directly and the stronger
`Equal` be stamped.

A pack that consumes an unpack has no lowering config of its own, so its
distribution hint is composed from the hints recorded on the two ops: the
unpack's distribution and `vector_common_parallel` hints together with the
pack's own `vector_common_parallel` hint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: scalable pack and unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax, a static
distribution tile of a scalable pack/unpack is a whole multiple of the
inner tile for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack/unpack fused into a packed-domain root such as an mmt4d takes its
distribution tile from the root's outer dims, so map that onto the
unpacked domain first. The result is itself scalable, which lets its
multiplier be compared against the inner tile's directly and the stronger
`Equal` be stamped.

A pack that consumes an unpack has no lowering config of its own, so its
distribution hint is composed from the hints recorded on the two ops: the
unpack's distribution and `vector_common_parallel` hints together with the
pack's own `vector_common_parallel` hint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax, a static
distribution tile of a scalable pack/unpack is a whole multiple of the
inner tile for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack/unpack fused into a packed-domain root such as an mmt4d takes its
distribution tile from the root's outer dims, so map that onto the
unpacked domain first. The result is itself scalable, which lets its
multiplier be compared against the inner tile's directly and the stronger
`Equal` be stamped.

distribution hint is composed from the hints recorded on the two ops: the
unpack's distribution and `vector_common_parallel` hints together with the
pack's own `vector_common_parallel` hint.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: scalable pack and unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax, a static
distribution tile of a scalable pack/unpack is a whole multiple of the
inner tile for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack/unpack fused into a packed-domain root such as an mmt4d takes its
distribution tile from the root's outer dims, so map that onto the
unpacked domain first. The result is itself scalable, which lets its
multiplier be compared against the inner tile's directly and the stronger
`Equal` be stamped.

A pack that consumes an unpack has no lowering config of its own, so its
distribution hint is composed from the hints recorded on the two ops: the
unpack's distribution and `vector_common_parallel` hints together with the
pack's own `vector_common_parallel` hint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: Analyze (python)

commit_message:
[ARM64] Add base bf16 mmt4d tiles for cores without the BF16 extension (#24900)

On Arm64 cores without the Armv8.6 BF16 extension, bf16 `mmt4d`
currently falls back to the scalar generic kernel. All existing Arm64
bf16 tiles require the `_bf16` feature:

```text
IREE_UK_MMT4D_TILE(arm_64, bf16, bf16, f32,  1..8, 8, 4, _bf16)
IREE_UK_MMT4D_TILE(arm_64, bf16, bf16, bf16, 1..8, 8, 4, _bf16)
```

This PR adds base Arm64 bf16 tiles for cores without that extension.

The new tiles widen bf16 operands to f32 using NEON, accumulate with
FMLA, and narrow back to bf16 on store when required. The same
implementation serves both bf16 and f32 accumulator/output variants.

No compiler changes are required: `enumerateMatmulTileArm64` already
selects `8x8x1` tiles for bf16 when the BF16 extension is unavailable.

## Performance

i.MX95 (Cortex-A55, six cores), 512x512x512, median of three runs:

| case | before | after | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 -> bf16 | 216 ms | 7.64 ms | 28x |
| bf16 -> f32 | 216 ms | 7.53 ms | 29x |
| f32 -> f32 | — | 8.22 ms | — |

For narrow M, using Mx512 by 512x512:

| M | before | after | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.52 ms | 0.879 ms | 1.7x |
| 2 | 2.31 ms | 0.874 ms | 2.6x |
| 4 | 3.37 ms | 0.887 ms | 3.8x |

## Correctness

Tested on device with `iree-run-module` for M=1,2,4,8 for bf16 -> bf16
and M=8 for bf16 -> f32.

The registered tiles match the generic implementation for normal inputs.
The widening behavior for bf16 subnormals and NaN payloads follows the
native NEON conversion behavior and can differ from the scalar helper,
similarly to the existing Arm64 f16 tiles.

The bf16 -> bf16 path accumulates in f32 and rounds once when storing,
matching the behavior of the existing Arm64 f16 tile.

Assisted by: Claude

---------

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax, a static
distribution tile of a scalable pack/unpack is a whole multiple of the
inner tile for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack/unpack fused into a packed-domain root such as an mmt4d takes its
distribution tile from the root's outer dims, so map that onto the
unpacked domain first. The result is itself scalable, which lets its
multiplier be compared against the inner tile's directly and the stronger
`Equal` be stamped.

A pack that consumes an unpack has no lowering config of its own, so its
distribution hint is composed from the hints recorded on the two ops: the
unpack's distribution and `vector_common_parallel` hints together with the
pack's own `vector_common_parallel` hint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: scalable pack and unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax, a static
distribution tile of a scalable pack/unpack is a whole multiple of the
inner tile for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack/unpack fused into a packed-domain root such as an mmt4d takes its
distribution tile from the root's outer dims, so map that onto the
unpacked domain first. The result is itself scalable, which lets its
multiplier be compared against the inner tile's directly and the stronger
`Equal` be stamped.

A pack that consumes an unpack has no lowering config of its own, so its
distribution hint is composed from the hints recorded on the two ops: the
unpack's distribution and `vector_common_parallel` hints together with the
pack's own `vector_common_parallel` hint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) to ensure correctness and
enable efficient tiling.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax, a static
distribution tile of a scalable pack/unpack is a whole multiple of the
inner tile for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack/unpack fused into a packed-domain root such as an mmt4d takes its
distribution tile from the root's outer dims, so map that onto the
unpacked domain first. The result is itself scalable, which lets its
multiplier be compared against the inner tile's directly and the stronger
`Equal` be stamped.

A pack that consumes an unpack has no lowering config of its own, so its
distribution hint is composed from the hints recorded on the two ops: the
unpack's distribution and `vector_common_parallel` hints together with the
pack's own `vector_common_parallel` hint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: scalable pack and unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

distribution tile of a scalable pack/unpack is a whole multiple of the
inner tile for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack/unpack fused into a packed-domain root such as an mmt4d takes its
distribution tile from the root's outer dims, so map that onto the
unpacked domain first. The result is itself scalable, which lets its
multiplier be compared against the inner tile's directly and the stronger
`Equal` be stamped.

A pack that consumes an unpack has no lowering config of its own, so its
distribution hint is composed from the hints recorded on the two ops: the
unpack's distribution and `vector_common_parallel` hints together with the
pack's own `vector_common_parallel` hint.

[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: scalable pack and unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: Analyze (actions)

`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: scalable pack and unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling), an mmt4d -> generic -> unpack -> pack chain that fuses into a
single workgroup forall with the scalable outer dim folded to a static 1, and a
dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing — the pack is only tiled
into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple relationship the driver
cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[ARM64] Add base bf16 mmt4d tiles for cores without the BF16 extension (#24900)

On Arm64 cores without the Armv8.6 BF16 extension, bf16 `mmt4d`
currently falls back to the scalar generic kernel. All existing Arm64
bf16 tiles require the `_bf16` feature:

```text
IREE_UK_MMT4D_TILE(arm_64, bf16, bf16, f32,  1..8, 8, 4, _bf16)
IREE_UK_MMT4D_TILE(arm_64, bf16, bf16, bf16, 1..8, 8, 4, _bf16)
```

This PR adds base Arm64 bf16 tiles for cores without that extension.

The new tiles widen bf16 operands to f32 using NEON, accumulate with
FMLA, and narrow back to bf16 on store when required. The same
implementation serves both bf16 and f32 accumulator/output variants.

No compiler changes are required: `enumerateMatmulTileArm64` already
selects `8x8x1` tiles for bf16 when the BF16 extension is unavailable.

## Performance

i.MX95 (Cortex-A55, six cores), 512x512x512, median of three runs:

| case | before | after | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 -> bf16 | 216 ms | 7.64 ms | 28x |
| bf16 -> f32 | 216 ms | 7.53 ms | 29x |
| f32 -> f32 | — | 8.22 ms | — |

For narrow M, using Mx512 by 512x512:

| M | before | after | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.52 ms | 0.879 ms | 1.7x |
| 2 | 2.31 ms | 0.874 ms | 2.6x |
| 4 | 3.37 ms | 0.887 ms | 3.8x |

## Correctness

Tested on device with `iree-run-module` for M=1,2,4,8 for bf16 -> bf16
and M=8 for bf16 -> f32.

The registered tiles match the generic implementation for normal inputs.
The widening behavior for bf16 subnormals and NaN payloads follows the
native NEON conversion behavior and can differ from the scalar helper,
similarly to the existing Arm64 f16 tiles.

The bf16 -> bf16 path accumulates in f32 and rounds once when storing,
matching the behavior of the existing Arm64 f16 tile.

Assisted by: Claude

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
publish_website: only publish from main, verify-only on release candidates

The Publish Website workflow is triggered by `release: [published,
unpublished]` events. Release candidate releases (tags like
`iree-3.6.0rc20250910`) go through the same path: the candidate release
workflows create a draft prerelease, Build Release Packages fills it, and
Validate and Publish Release publishes it -- which fires the `published`
event and made Publish Website deploy the site from the RC, overwriting
whatever main had last published (losing a blogpost recently).

Keep running the site build steps as verification, but skip the
gh-pages deployment when the run was triggered by a release candidate
release. Deployment still happens for main pushes, schedules, manual
dispatches, and stable releases.

Fixes #24764

Signed-off-by: linsen <linsen@insta360.com>
name: pr-greeter

[GlobalOptimization] Propagate QDQ through layout operations

Move quantize toward real-valued producers and dequantize toward contraction consumers before rewriting QDQ contractions to integer math.

Reuse reshape expansion and unit-dimension folding for affine quantization ops, and handle dequantize transpose and zero-pad consumers with explicit legality checks.

commit_message:
[ARM64] Add base bf16 mmt4d tiles for cores without the BF16 extension (#24900)

On Arm64 cores without the Armv8.6 BF16 extension, bf16 `mmt4d`
currently falls back to the scalar generic kernel. All existing Arm64
bf16 tiles require the `_bf16` feature:

```text
IREE_UK_MMT4D_TILE(arm_64, bf16, bf16, f32,  1..8, 8, 4, _bf16)
IREE_UK_MMT4D_TILE(arm_64, bf16, bf16, bf16, 1..8, 8, 4, _bf16)
```

This PR adds base Arm64 bf16 tiles for cores without that extension.

The new tiles widen bf16 operands to f32 using NEON, accumulate with
FMLA, and narrow back to bf16 on store when required. The same
implementation serves both bf16 and f32 accumulator/output variants.

No compiler changes are required: `enumerateMatmulTileArm64` already
selects `8x8x1` tiles for bf16 when the BF16 extension is unavailable.

## Performance

i.MX95 (Cortex-A55, six cores), 512x512x512, median of three runs:

| case | before | after | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 -> bf16 | 216 ms | 7.64 ms | 28x |
| bf16 -> f32 | 216 ms | 7.53 ms | 29x |
| f32 -> f32 | — | 8.22 ms | — |

For narrow M, using Mx512 by 512x512:

| M | before | after | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.52 ms | 0.879 ms | 1.7x |
| 2 | 2.31 ms | 0.874 ms | 2.6x |
| 4 | 3.37 ms | 0.887 ms | 3.8x |

## Correctness

Tested on device with `iree-run-module` for M=1,2,4,8 for bf16 -> bf16
and M=8 for bf16 -> f32.

The registered tiles match the generic implementation for normal inputs.
The widening behavior for bf16 subnormals and NaN payloads follows the
native NEON conversion behavior and can differ from the scalar helper,
similarly to the existing Arm64 f16 tiles.

The bf16 -> bf16 path accumulates in f32 and rounds once when storing,
matching the behavior of the existing Arm64 f16 tile.

On Arm64 cores without the Armv8.6 BF16 extension, bf16 `mmt4d`
currently falls back to the scalar generic kernel. All existing Arm64
bf16 tiles require the `_bf16` feature:

```text
IREE_UK_MMT4D_TILE(arm_64, bf16, bf16, f32,  1..8, 8, 4, _bf16)
IREE_UK_MMT4D_TILE(arm_64, bf16, bf16, bf16, 1..8, 8, 4, _bf16)
```

This PR adds base Arm64 bf16 tiles for cores without that extension.

The new tiles widen bf16 operands to f32 using NEON, accumulate with
FMLA, and narrow back to bf16 on store when required. The same
implementation serves both bf16 and f32 accumulator/output variants.

No compiler changes are required: `enumerateMatmulTileArm64` already
selects `8x8x1` tiles for bf16 when the BF16 extension is unavailable.

## Performance

i.MX95 (Cortex-A55, six cores), 512x512x512, median of three runs:

| case | before | after | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 -> bf16 | 216 ms | 7.64 ms | 28x |
| bf16 -> f32 | 216 ms | 7.53 ms | 29x |
| f32 -> f32 | — | 8.22 ms | — |

For narrow M, using Mx512 by 512x512:

| M | before | after | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.52 ms | 0.879 ms | 1.7x |
| 2 | 2.31 ms | 0.874 ms | 2.6x |
| 4 | 3.37 ms | 0.887 ms | 3.8x |

## Correctness

Tested on device with `iree-run-module` for M=1,2,4,8 for bf16 -> bf16
and M=8 for bf16 -> f32.

The registered tiles match the generic implementation for normal inputs.
The widening behavior for bf16 subnormals and NaN payloads follows the
native NEON conversion behavior and can differ from the scalar helper,
similarly to the existing Arm64 f16 tiles.

The bf16 -> bf16 path accumulates in f32 and rounds once when storing,
matching the behavior of the existing Arm64 f16 tile.

currently falls back to the scalar generic kernel. All existing Arm64
bf16 tiles require the `_bf16` feature:

```text

```

This PR adds base Arm64 bf16 tiles for cores without that extension.

FMLA, and narrow back to bf16 on store when required. The same
implementation serves both bf16 and f32 accumulator/output variants.

No compiler changes are required: `enumerateMatmulTileArm64` already
selects `8x8x1` tiles for bf16 when the BF16 extension is unavailable.

i.MX95 (Cortex-A55, six cores), 512x512x512, median of three runs:

| case | before | after | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 -> bf16 | 216 ms | 7.64 ms | 28x |
| bf16 -> f32 | 216 ms | 7.53 ms | 29x |

| M | before | after | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|

[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-

blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Drop a provably zero zero_point from the quantization ops

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Drop a provably zero zero_point from the quantization ops

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Signed-off-by: default <ziereis@roofline.ai>

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Drop a provably zero zero_point from the quantization ops

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its

tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Drop a provably zero zero_point from the quantization ops

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Signed-off-by: default <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Drop a provably zero zero_point from the quantization ops

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Signed-off-by: default <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
